messages:
customer-jdoe: Hey team — our Vercel Edge app using @redwood/sdk v0.9.1 keeps stalling mid-stream. Happens intermittently but reproducible for us, usually around ~3-5s into a long SSE response.

elena: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro and any logs? is this only on Vercel Edge or also in Node server env?

customer-jdoe: repro steps:
1) deploy to Vercel edge (node 18 runtime)
2) code:
```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const res = await client.responses.stream({ model: 'redwood-stream', input: 'long output test' });
const reader = res.body?.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader!.read();
  if (done) break;
  process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```
Logs: we see initial 200, then a sudden close and a reader error: 
```
200 OK /v1/responses/stream
Chunked: first 8 tokens
TypeError: Failed to read from 'ReadableStreamDefaultReader': The underlying source has been canceled.
at async readLoop (edge-handler:45:12)
```
We also noticed occasional 401 immediately followed by a reconnect and then two identical chunks, so duplicates appear.

matt: sounds like two issues: (A) reader cancel on edge runtime; (B) token rotation + retry logic causing duplicate chunks. are you rotating your RW token in-app?

customer-jdoe: we rotate short-lived keys via our auth proxy, yes. but behavior didn't happen when we tested on a regular Node server — only edge.

elena: can you share the exact sdk version lock? package.json entry?

customer-jdoe: "@redwood/sdk": "0.9.1"

jonah: quick heads up — eng-runtime recently shipped a patch for token-refresh backoff on streaming in 0.9.3/0.9.4. v0.9.1 had a bug where the edge getReader polyfill would call cancel() on network disconnect without retry backoff, which can surface as "underlying source has been canceled". also retry logic could spawn overlapping reconnects if a 401 occurred during an inflight stream.

devex: can you try upgrading to 0.9.4 and re-test? That release fixes: improved backoff on reconnect, dedupe on retry-on-auth, and a safer cancel path for edge runtimes.

customer-jdoe: we can't upgrade production right now — do you have a short-term workaround?

matt: a few options:
- temporary: disable streaming for that route (stream: false) so you get whole-response semantics.
- work-around: add a short client-side guard to ignore duplicate chunk prefixes (dedupe by sequence id if you can inject one).
- if you can deploy a tiny serverless node lambda (non-edge) as proxy, it seems not affected.

elena: if you can share a small zipped repro or a staging URL, we can test the upgrade on your app (we can spin a quick PR for you).

customer-jdoe: tried a quick test locally upgrading to 0.9.4 on my laptop — streaming looks stable so far, no cancel errors. Will try staging in Vercel later tonight.

support-bot: Escalation created: SEV-3 stream-retry-edge-1832509876, assigned to eng-runtime.

jonah: for the team: root cause summary in case we need internal notes — v0.9.1: edgeReadable polyfill called reader.cancel() on socket close before proper backoff, and retry-on-401 could spawn reconnect without coordinating inflight stream cancellation. Duplicate payloads when reconnect overlapped. fixed in 0.9.3+ with coordination token-refresh lock and linear backoff.

elena: thanks — @customer-jdoe please confirm after staging test. if upgrade fixes it we'll close; if not we'll request a quick repro and eng will attach a hotfix. :thumbsup:

customer-jdoe: confirmed after Vercel staging deploy to 0.9.4 — streaming no longer stalls and duplicates gone. will schedule a full prod rollout tomorrow. thanks all! :raised_hands:

matt: great — marking resolved for now. If anything else shows up, reopen thread.
